sentences.text: This claim petition is filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .25,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by her in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 20.05.2023 at about 01.00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in Honda Activa Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-13-ER-2213 on left side of road, near Mangala Village, SH-84 Sira to Nanjanagudu Road, Yadiyur Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District,
another Suzuki Access Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HM-2677, ridden by its rider at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, dashed to the petitioner.

Due to the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter, she was shifted to AIMS Hospital at G.Nagar, wherein she took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .7,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing Tailoring and cloth business and was earning .30,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of motor cycle by its rider.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

3. In pursuance of notice, though respondent No.1 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel,
he has not filed the written statement.
Respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that front portion of both got damaged which indicates that the accident occurred from head on collusion and as such, there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of honda activa vehicle.
Further the owner of suzuki bike has not immediately reported the occurrence of accident to this respondent.
Further contended that the rider was riding the suzuki bike without possessing valid and effective driving license, FC as on the date of accident.
Further contended that two wheeler in which the petitioner is stated to be proceeding was not having policy and was not having valid DL.
Further the petitioner drove the vehicle negligently without observing the vehicular traffic at the time of accident.
The petitioner was riding the scooter without wearing the helmet.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HM-2677 by its rider, in RTA took place on 20.05.2023 at about 01.00 p.m., on SH-84 Kavya K.R vs Basavaraju A.Y on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35489840/
2

Sira-Nanjanagudu Road, Near Mangala Village, Yadeyuru Hobli, Kunigal Taluk,
Tumakuru?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6.

In order to prove the contention of the petition, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1, got examined Record Technician at Adichunchanagiri Hospital as PW.2, one eyewitness by name Sri.Razik as PW.3 and Dr.S.A.Somashekara, Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW.4 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16 and closed evidence of her side.

On the other hand, the CMO, Adichunchanagiri Hospital examined as RW.1 and MRO of Adichunchanagiri Hospital examined as RW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.3 and closed their side of evidence.

7. Heard the arguments of both the side and perused the materials available on record.
8.

Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are under:-
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:-
-:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 20.05.2023 at about 01.00 p.m., accident occurred near Mangala Village SH-84, Sira-Nanjanagudu Road, Yadiyuru Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District, when petitioner was proceeding in Honda Active Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-13-ER-2213, due to the rash and negligent riding of Suzuki Access Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HM-2677, by its rider in which she sustained grievous injuries.
10.
Further, in order to prove accident, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.2, first information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.2, first information statement, one of the relatives of petitioner by name Sri.Arun Kumar K.P has lodged complaint with police on 21.05.2023 pertaining to the accident occurred on 20.05.2023.
The police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable under Sec.279 & 337 of IPC.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent riding of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.1 discloses the aspect of registration of FIR against the rider of offending motor cycle.
11. The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar, which is marked as Ex.P.3.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said documents.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.

Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report, wherein Kavya K.R vs Basavaraju A.Y on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35489840/
3 damages caused to both the vehicles are mentioned.
The vehicle will be inspected by the concerned authority after seizure of the same by the police.
The IMV report indicates the aspect of seizure of offending vehicle on the ground of its involvement in the accident.
The rider or owner of the offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the seizure procedure conducted by the police.
Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate, which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
12. The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the rider of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC as per Ex.P.6.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in proper manner.
The rider or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of rider of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
13. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondent not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of records, it discloses that accident was caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.

Under these circumstances,
relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.6,
this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HM-2677 by its rider and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:
The petitioner succeeded in establishing that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent riding of offending vehicle.
As Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

The Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses,
food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment,
disability, loss of amenities etc., in order to assess the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled.

i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident she sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to Kavya K.R vs Basavaraju A.Y on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35489840/
4 take follow up treatment.

In order to prove the injuries sustained in the accident, the petitioner produced Wound certificate issued by Adichunchanagiri Hospital &
Research Centre marked at Ex.P.5.
The said document discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature.

The petitioner also furnished discharge summary which is marked as Ex.P.8 and said document discloses the aspect of availing treatment at the hospital by her for the injuries sustained in the accident.
Further, the petitioner examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara. as PW.4 and got marked Ex.P.15 & 16 documents.
PW.4/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of permanent physical disability and assessed disability to the left lower limb at 62% and to whole body at 31%.
On consideration of the materials placed before the Tribunal, compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards Pain and Suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:-
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that she took treatment at the Hospital.
The petitioner has produced medical bills for a sum of .1,77,983/- marked at Ex.P.9.
In the medical bills furnished as serial No.12, 13 and 14, there is mention about Corporate name as Arogya Karnataka Scheme.
The respondents contended that entire medical expenses have been disbursed under the said scheme and the petitioner is not entitled for medical expenses.
The respondents got examined concerned person from Adichunchanagiri hospital as RW.2.
RW.2 stated that only .5,000/- has been disbursed under Arogya Karnataka scheme towards medical expenses of the petitioner and entire amount has not been disbursed.
Further, the medical bills furnished before the Tribunal do not indicate the aspect of payment of entire medical expenses under Arogya Karnataka scheme.
RW.2 clearly deposed before the Tribunal that only .5,000/- has been disbursed towards the medical expenses under the scheme and remaining medical expense has been paid by petitioner.
RW.2 furnished document in that regard which is marked as Ex.R.3 which discloses the aspect of disbursement of .5,000/- towards the medical expenses.

The respondents cross examined RW.2,
but nothing to substantiate their contention could be elicited in the cross examination.

No satisfactory materials are placed before the Tribunal to show that entire medical expenses of the petitioner has been disbursed under Arogya Karnataka scheme and petitioner has not paid any amount towards medical expenses.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said document.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also, nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.

As per the documents furnished before the tribunal, the total medical expenses incurred by petitioner is .1,77,983/- and out of said amount, a sum of .5,000/- is disbursed under Arogya Karnataka Scheme.
The sum disbursed towards medical expenses under the scheme is to be deducted from the compensation that will be awarded towards medical expenses.

Thus, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .1,72,983/-
appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:- On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 20.05.2023 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient in the hospital.
On perusal of materials on record, the petitioner appears to have admitted as an inpatient at Hospital pertaining to the injuries sustained by her and availed treatment as an inpatient.

So, during Kavya K.R vs Basavaraju A.Y on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35489840/
5
the time of treatment the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.8, Discharge Summaries issued by Adichunchanagiri Hospital &
Research Center, which discloses the aspect of availing treatment by petitioner as an inpatient from 20.05.2023 to 24.06.2023 i.e., for a period of 35 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 35 days to a sum of .17,500/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.
(iv) Towards Conveyance:-

The petitioner is the resident of Kothanahalli Village, Hirisave Hobli,
Channarayapattna Taluk, Hassan District and she admitted to hospital for availing treatment.
In order to prove the said aspect, the petitioner has produced discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.8.
The petitioner might have incurred expenses for conveyance during the period of treatment.
Considering the injuries sustained and facts of the case, the tribunal is of view that the compensation of .10,000/- appears just and proper towards conveyance charges.

(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:-
The petitioner contended that she was doing Tailoring and cloth business and earning a sum of .30,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income, the petitioner not produced any documents.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials to show that she was earning .30,000/- per month.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to substantiate her contention regarding occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as .16,000/-.

On perusal of records,
it appears that petitioner might have not attended her work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .40,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.

(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:-
The petitioner contended that due to accident, she was admitted as an inpatient at Hospital and sustained permanent disablement.
The petitioner also examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara, working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital as PW.4.
PW.4/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.

The doctor deposed that petitioner has sustained distal third fracture of left femur,
open type II fracture of both bones of left leg, fracture distal third left fibula and type III B open fracture shaft of 2nd metatarsal left foot and underwent surgeries in the form of CRIF with IMIL hailing of left femur, CRIF with IMIL hailing of left tibia,
ORIF with K-wiring and CC screw for 2nd metatarsal and lateral malleolus fracture,
tendon repair, debridement and NPWT for left fore and split skin grafting for left foot and later discharged.

Further petitioner complains of pain and difficulty in walking Kavya K.R vs Basavaraju A.Y on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35489840/
6 and climbing stairs, inability to squat and sit cross legged, inability to squat and sit cross legged and inability to work as a tailor cum clothes merchant.

Further PW.4 in his chief examination deposed that on examination, petitioner walks with pain and limping, wasting of left thigh and swelling of left leg is seen, surgical scars are seen over left hip thigh knee & leg, scars are seen over left foot.

Further deposed that on recent X-ray revealed that united fracture femur with implants in situ, uniting fracture tibia with implants in situ, mal-united segmental fractures of fibula and united fracture 2nd metatarsal with 2 CC screws in situ.
The doctor assessed the disability to the left lower limb at 62% and to the whole body at 31%.
In order to prove the disability, the doctor has produced recent assessment OPD report and X-ray marked at Ex.P.15 & 16.
PW.4 not stated that the petitioner could not be able to do her routine activities in a normal way.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that the petitioner is unable to do any work at all.
The injuries sustained by petitioner do not appear to cause much problem in doing her activities.

The petitioner also examined Record Technician at Adichunchnagiri Hospital as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P.11 to 14 i.e., authorization letter, MLC,
Police intimation and inpatient case details.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do her work with difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 20%.

sentences.text: In order to prove the age, the petitioner has produced Ex.P.7 - Notarized copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein her date of birth is shown as 10.04.1995.
The accident occurred on 20.05.2023.
As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner appears to be 28 years as on the date of accident.
The respondents not furnished satisfactory materials in order to doubt or rebut the document furnished by petitioner related to age.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by petitioner is to be considered for ascertaining the age of petitioner.
As per the document furnished by petitioner, her age is 28 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
As per Smt.Sarla Verma case multiplier applicable is '17'.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s.
Ajay Kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of her gross income.

Hence, future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under :
Annual Income before accident : (.16,000/- x 12) = .1,92,000/-
 Loss of future earning p.a. (20% of prior annual  income) = .38,400/-.

Kavya K.R vs Basavaraju A.Y on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35489840/
7 Multiplier applicable with reference to age - 17 Loss of future earnings - (.38,400/- x 17) = .6,52,800/-.
The petitioner is entitled for .6,52,800/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
(vii) Deprivation of Future Amenities:- The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and she is unable to do her day- today activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.

(viii) Towards Future Medical Expenses:
The doctor/PW.4 has opined that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant the estimate of the surgery is around .60,000/-.
The petitioner not furnished satisfactory materials in order to substantiate the said aspect.
The petitioner not furnished materials in order to show the cost of future surgery.
The cost stated by PW.4 for future surgery is not substantiated by any satisfactory materials.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case .30,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future medical expenses.

sentences.text: 17. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-06-HM-2677 by its rider.
So, the respondents being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.

18. Issue No.3:- In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .9,83,283/- (Rupees Nine Lakhs Eighty Three Thousand Two Hundred and Eighty Three only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
(future medical expenses shall not carry any interest)
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of her Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of rider of offending vehicle.
No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondent not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
On perusal of records, it discloses that accident was caused due to negligence on the part of rider of offending vehicle.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, notional income is to be taken into consideration.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .40,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
The accident occurred on 20.05.2023.
As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner appears to be 28 years as on the date of accident.
The respondents not furnished satisfactory materials in order to doubt or rebut the document furnished by petitioner related to age.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the document furnished by petitioner is to be considered for ascertaining the age of petitioner.
As per the document furnished by petitioner, her age is 28 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
Ajay Kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of her gross income.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.
